svg.title: Four web vulnerability families and the interpreter each one abuses
svg.desc: Three panels. Injection and cross-site scripting: string concatenation into a parser, and script injected into the browser DOM, remediated by parameterized queries and context-aware encoding. SSRF and insecure deserialization: the server coerced into fetching an internal metadata endpoint, and untrusted object streams running gadget chains, remediated by destination allowlisting with IMDSv2 and by safe data formats. Memory safety: the four corruption classes, what Rust and Go change, and the C and C plus plus hardening flags, with a footer noting that the guarantee covers safe-subset code only.
svg.text: Untrusted data reaching an interpreter
Each family below is the same failure against a different parser. The control is structural separation, not filtering.
INJECTION AND CROSS-SITE SCRIPTING
Interpreter: SQL parser, OS shell, browser HTML parser
SQL / command injection: input concatenated into text that is later parsed.
XSS: reflected, stored, or DOM-based script executing inside the origin.
Control
Bind query values; pass an argument vector with no shell; encode
for the exact insertion context and use safe DOM sinks.
SSRF AND INSECURE DESERIALIZATION
Interpreter: URL fetcher, object deserializer
SSRF: the server coerced into fetching 169.254.169.254 or an
internal service. In the 2025 list this sits under A01 access control.
Deserialization: untrusted object streams running gadget chains.
Control
Allowlist the destination, re-check the resolved IP, block redirects,
enforce IMDSv2; parse data-only formats into a declared schema.
MEMORY SAFETY UNDER THE WEB STACK
Interpreter: the machine itself — TLS terminators, image and font parsers, XML libraries
Four classes: buffer overflow (spatial), use-after-free (temporal), double free, null pointer dereference.
Rust removes them at compile time through ownership and borrowing; Go through garbage collection and bounds checks.
Legacy C / C++ hardening: PIE and ASLR, NX, stack protector, RELRO, _FORTIFY_SOURCE, control-flow integrity.
The memory-safety guarantee covers safe-subset code only. Rust unsafe blocks, FFI and cgo boundaries, and Go data races all reintroduce it.
AddressSanitizer is a testing instrumentation with roughly 2x slowdown — it belongs in CI, not in a shipped binary.
